newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S SANLAM SEES RAND AT 4.65 VS DLR IN Q4.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S SANLAM SEES RAND AT 4.65 VS DLR IN Q4.

text.p: Sanlam chief economist Jac Laubscher said on Thursday he expected the rand to average about 4.65 to the dollar in the fourth quarter of 1997 while this year's current account deficit should fall to around six billion rand.

Laubscher said in an economic commentary the stabilisation of the rand after its sharp fall in 1996 had contributed to increased net foreign purchases of South African bonds and equities totalling 9.5 billion rand in the first quarter.
"We are, however, concerned that a situation such as that prevailing at the end of 1995, when the rand became overvalued, should not be allowed to develop again.
"The authorities should therefore use any opportunity offered by a strong rand to take further steps to normalise South Africa's external financial relations," he said.
Laubscher said Sanlam did not believe that the relaxation of foreign exchange controls promised in Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's March budget would put the rand under stress.
The concessions included permission for individuals to hold some foreign currency in South Africa or abroad and a more liberal application of the 10 percent limit on institutional investments abroad.
Laubscher said the rand had appreciated against currencies including those of India, Malaysia, China and Brazil which could constrain export growth.

"Notwithstanding, we are forecasting that the deficit on the current account of the balance of payments will reduce from last year's approximately 8.5 billion rand to a deficit of approximately six billion rand in 1997.
"The improvement in the current account balance will also contribute to greater stability in the external value of the rand," he said.
